question: is the -1.010% indentation plateau at depth 96a truncation or model bias?
reference: Hertz 1882 J. reine angew. Math. 92:156; Johnson 1985 Contact Mechanics 4.2 DOI:10.1017/cbo9781139171731

environment.note: far-field mesh stretched, not re-refined: element count constant with depth

contact_radius.blocked: truncation_insensitive: the spread over the whole depth ladder is 0.0010 pp <= 0.05 pp, i.e. this quantity barely sees the truncation boundary and must not be extrapolated

peak_pressure.blocked: truncation_insensitive: the spread over the whole depth ladder is 0.0005 pp <= 0.05 pp, i.e. this quantity barely sees the truncation boundary and must not be extrapolated

contact_radius.blocked: truncation_insensitive: the spread over the whole depth ladder is 0.0001 pp <= 0.05 pp, i.e. this quantity barely sees the truncation boundary and must not be extrapolated

peak_pressure.blocked: truncation_insensitive: the spread over the whole depth ladder is 0.0002 pp <= 0.05 pp, i.e. this quantity barely sees the truncation boundary and must not be extrapolated

decision.hypothesis: H_trunc: the -1.010% indentation plateau at depth 96a is an unconverged truncation error, i.e. |e_inf(delta)| <= 0.5% at infinite depth with a monotone decay of observed order in [0.5, 3]
decision.alternative: H_bias: the offset survives an infinite domain; the extrapolated residual is then reported as a (small) model bias of the Q4-paraboloid model

gate_table.quantity: |e_inf(delta)|: Richardson limit of the indentation error as depth/ a -> inf (a/R = 0.05, h/a = 0.015)
gate_table.reference: delta = a^2/R (Hertz 1882; Johnson 1985 §4.2) at infinite half-space

gate_table.quantity: |e_inf(delta)| against the pre-declared 0.5% bound that separates 'unconverged truncation' from 'model bias'
gate_table.reference: H_trunc accepted iff the extrapolated residual is <= 0.5%
gate_table.note: a FAIL here is a *result*, not an error: it quantifies the irreducible model bias of the Q4 paraboloid model (see verdict in truncation_extrapolation.json)

gate_table.quantity: number of levels where the indentation error does NOT decay in magnitude towards the infinite-domain limit
gate_table.reference: a truncation error must vanish as the boundary recedes

gate_table.quantity: |observed decay order of the indentation-error sequence| (depth doubling)
gate_table.reference: admissible band [0.5, 3]; an order far below the band means the ladder is still in the pre-asymptotic regime

gate_table.quantity: spread (pp) of |contact-radius error| over the depth ladder 96a -> 768a
gate_table.reference: the contact radius is a near-field measure: if the depth ladder moves it, the reported a is contaminated by truncation
delta = a^2/R at infinite half-space; load independence of the plateau is what made it look mesh-independent
